# Skarra

## Personality

Stern, watchful and dryly funny once the patrol is safely home.

## Lore

Skarra commands the Uskari trail watch, the patrols that guard Midbarium's highland trails, drive off the monsters that come up from the canyons and see travelers safely from one camp to the next. She is forty-one, stern and watchful on the trail, and nobody on the rim has ever heard her laugh while a patrol is still out. Once every patrol is safely home, she turns out to be the driest wit on the rim, and the scouts who have learned this stay late at her fire on purpose.

### The watch

Skarra was born on the Uskari Rim and was tracking goats along the canyon edges before she was ten. She never left to adventure, as so many young Uskari do; she says she could see all the trouble she wanted from the rim. She joined the trail watch at sixteen, became its best tracker by twenty-five, and was made its captain ten years ago by Hask, then chieftain of the Uskari, who chose her because she was the only scout who reported bad news before good.

She has served under two chieftains since. When Hask was chosen Old One six years ago, the Uskari chose Tavi, and Tavi doubled the patrols. Skarra approved of the doubling and argued with every route Tavi drew for it. The two of them have been friendly rivals since Tavi came home from adventuring, nearly twenty years ago, in everything from climbing races to arguments about patrol routes. Tavi still walks the worst stretch of trail personally, and Skarra has given up trying to stop it; she simply makes sure the scout walking behind Tavi is a good one.

### The hide map

In her tent, Skarra keeps a hide map of the highlands, painted with every trail, camp, bridge and cave the watch knows. Since the day she became captain she has marked every monster sighting on it with a dot of red ochre and the date. Ten years ago the dots sat mostly in the low valleys and the far canyons. Each season since, they have crept a little closer to town. This summer there are dots on the high pastures, on the south path and at the far end of the far canyon bridge.

She shows the map to Tavi and to no one else. In council the Uskari report that the trails are held, and they are; but Skarra knows exactly how few scouts are holding them, and she has stopped sending hunters out to the far slopes for game, hides or Lessa's grey herb, because she cannot spare them.

### Bekk

Skarra's son Bekk is eighteen, cocky, quick and the fastest climber on the rim, with a crowd of admiring children at his heels. His father, Haldo, went out alone onto the far slopes thirteen years ago to track a great horned beast and was gored and killed by it, and Skarra raised Bekk on the rim among the patrols. She is harder on him than on any scout she commands, and she knows he knows why.

Now Bekk wants to track the beast that has been raiding the high pastures, and he wants to do it alone. Skarra has forbidden it. She has not told him that she has measured the beast's tracks herself, and that they frighten her.

When Dorrek of the Kragvar came to her quietly last month to ask how young the Uskari take recruits, she told him sixteen, and asked whether this was about his small son who follows Bekk everywhere. Dorrek said it was a general question. Skarra has been smiling about it ever since, though only after dark.

### The stretch nobody walks

Skarra has noticed that Ketta, who came home last spring, always trades away the stretch of canyon trail that passes a certain deep cave. Skarra has let her, and has said nothing. But that stretch has a red dot on it now.

A quest could help Skarra check the newest dots on her map before the next council, or walk the canyon stretch Ketta will not.
